decided.claim: Record a new top-level `panes = <n>` scalar in StateFile on every save, sourced from the existing pane_count(); Option<usize> with serde default + skip_serializing_if so old files load and old builds ignore it.

Demote via an effective save time rather than a hard tier: a known-trivial session competes as if saved TRIVIAL_HANDICAP (7 days) earlier, so the gap is measured between the two saves, never against now — a vacation ages both equally, order stays total, and trivial sessions keep newest-first among themselves.
Trivial means panes <= 1 (TRIVIAL_MAX_PANES): one split is already a deliberate arrangement, and the demotion stays narrow because demoting wrongly is the ticket's headline bug in reverse.

Compatibility by polarity: only sessions KNOWN trivial are handicapped; a file with no panes key (pre-upgrade, incl. legacy state.toml adoption) gets Candidate.panes = None and ranks exactly as today, so upgrading demotes nobody.

Read the count with toml_top_level_integer, a sibling of the existing hand-rolled toml_top_level_string, off the single read_to_string the scan already performs — no TOML deserialisation added to the boot path.

The workspace hint stays the untouched primary sort key; the handicap only replaces the recency term below it, so a session you were standing on wins however small it is, and in the ticket's same-workspace story the hint ties and the handicap decides.
theme_key_in (the scratch tear-off look) keeps sharing rank(), so a scratch window now borrows the arranged session's look over a newer throwaway's — one ranking doctrine rather than two.

Tests: pure rank() cases for the story, the opposite-failure guard, the hint's supremacy, the pre-upgrade guarantee, the 2-pane boundary, trivial-vs-trivial recency, plus the parser unit test and an end-to-end file-based adoption of the story on a tied workspace hint.

least_confident.why: The 7-day handicap is a judgment call between the same-day throwaway (minutes-hours) and the forbidden weeks-long stickiness; 48h was the plausible alternative and I erred long because wrongly burying the wall is the headline harm, but a wall idle 6 days still beating a day-old single pane may annoy someone.
A 2-pane quickie still bulldozes the wall under this threshold; the brief's story is literally one pane so I kept the line narrow, but 'trivial' could defensibly include 2 panes or 1 tab.

A scratch torn off from the throwaway itself now borrows the wall's look instead of its actual parent's when their workspaces differ; the hint rescues the common case, but I chose doctrine-sharing over special-casing without being able to observe it.

not_done.claim: toml 0.8 emitting `panes` in the top-level scalar section (before the first [table] header) is unverified at runtime.
not_done.why: Argued by analogy: last_workspace is the struct's last field yet provably lands top-level (the existing hand-parser and its fixtures depend on it), and toml 0.8 orders values before tables; a running app would confirm.

not_done.claim: No absolute-age decay: adoption never compares against now, so a wall idle 6 days still beats yesterday's throwaway.
not_done.why: Deliberate — the brief bounds stickiness at 'weeks', and save-to-save comparison is vacation-safe where a now-relative horizon is not.

not_done.claim: No richer weight than pane count (tabs, agents, named panes not consulted).
not_done.why: Pane count is the one cheap honest signal the story needs; anything more would widen the file format for speculative benefit.
